summary: The study describes the atomic-layer chemical-vapor deposition (ALD) of silicon dioxide (SiO2) with an extremely low hydrogen content using tetra-iso-cyanate-silane (TICS) and tertiary-ethyl-amine (TEA) as precursors. The process was carried out at 150 8C, and the deposition rate was found to be independent of the exposure times of the precursors, with a saturated deposition rate of about 1.2 A/cycle. The film exhibited low surface roughness and minimal hydrogen content, making it suitable for applications in ULSI technology.
evidence: We achieved the atomic-layer-deposition of SiO with an extremely low H content for the first time by using Si NCO2 4 and N C H . The saturated deposition rate was about 1.2 A rcycle at 150 8C. AFM observation revealed that the increase of roughness after 50 deposition cycles was only about 0.4 A in root mean square. The FT-IR spectra showed that the deposited film was SiO without Si±H, Si±OH or NCO bond.
